guarantees.claim: prd_clearing_data is always assigned the value of prd_clearing_128[0].
prd_clearing_state is always assigned the full 128-bit value of prd_clearing_128.
prd_clearing_key is always assigned the full 256-bit value of prd_clearing_256.
cipher_op_buf is always driven by the type-cast of cipher_op_raw to ciph_op_e.
When SecMasking is 0, state_init[0] is the bitwise XOR of state_in and add_state_in.
When SecMasking is 0, state_out is the bitwise XOR of state_done_buf[0] and state_done_buf[1].
data_in_prev_sel is always driven by the type-cast of data_in_prev_sel_raw to dip_sel_e.
state_in_sel is always driven by the type-cast of state_in_sel_raw to si_sel_e.
add_state_in_sel is always driven by the type-cast of add_state_in_sel_raw to add_si_sel_e.
add_state_out_sel is always driven by the type-cast of add_state_out_sel_raw to add_so_sel_e.
key_init_sel is always driven by the type-cast of key_init_sel_raw to key_init_sel_e.
sp2v_sig at the index NumSharesKey * NumRegsKey + NumSlicesCtr is always driven by data_in_prev_we_ctrl.
sp2v_sig at the index NumSharesKey * NumRegsKey + NumSlicesCtr + 1 is always driven by data_out_we_ctrl.
unused_alert_signals is always driven by the reduction XOR of all bits of reg2hw.alert_test.

assumptions.claim: NumSp2VSig must be at least (NumSharesKey * NumRegsKey + NumSlicesCtr + 1) so that the assigned indices of sp2v_sig are within its declared bounds.
assumptions.cond: always, based on static parameter values
assumptions.risk: If violated, the assignment writes to an out-of-range index, causing simulation errors (X or out-of-bounds access) and potential synthesis mismatch.

assumptions.claim: data_in_prev_sel_raw, state_in_sel_raw, add_state_in_sel_raw, add_state_out_sel_raw, and key_init_sel_raw must carry bit patterns that correspond to valid members of their respective enum types.
assumptions.cond: whenever these raw signals are evaluated
assumptions.risk: If an invalid bit pattern is present, the type-cast produces an unknown (X) value, potentially propagating X to critical control paths and breaking the FSM or data selection.

assumptions.claim: prd_clearing_128 and prd_clearing_256 must be properly driven with intended clearing values; otherwise the assigned clearing data/state/key may not achieve a full wipe.
assumptions.cond: when clearing is initiated by external logic
assumptions.risk: Incomplete or missing clearing could leave sensitive key/state/data residual values, violating security guarantees.

uncertain_points.claim: sp2v_sig is a wide vector (NumSp2VSig bits), but within this chunk only two specific bits are assigned. It is unknown whether the remaining bits are driven elsewhere or left floating.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven bits could be synthesized to constant 0 or 1, causing incorrect single-rail conversion of critical control signals and potentially breaking masked security logic.

uncertain_points.claim: prng_reseed_rate_q is declared but never assigned or used in this chunk; its purpose and driving logic are external.
uncertain_points.risk: If genuinely unused, it represents dead code; if expected to be driven, missing connection could cause X propagation in PRNG reseed rate control.

uncertain_points.claim: sp2v_sig_chk is declared with the same dimensions as sp2v_sig but is never assigned in this chunk; its intended role (checking/monitoring) is unclear.
uncertain_points.risk: If left undriven, any downstream comparison using sp2v_sig_chk may silently pass or fail, hiding sp2v conversion errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The assignments to sp2v_sig rely on the arithmetic expression NumSharesKey * NumRegsKey + NumSlicesCtr. If any of these parameters are zero or configured such that the sum exceeds NumSp2VSig-1, an out-of-bounds write occurs.
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-bounds write may cause simulation errors or silent synthesis mismatch, corrupting unrelated logic or masking critical control signals.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_alert_signals is defined as the XOR of alert_test bits, but its name suggests it exists to satisfy lint/tie-off rules. The XOR behavior may mask individual alert test activations (e.g., even number of 1's produces 0).
uncertain_points.risk: If this signal is inadvertently used for actual alert monitoring, it could fail to detect certain alert patterns; if only used as a dummy read, no functional risk.
